title: The Bridge Gives Way
text: The great bridge, older than any House, groans in the night and drops a span into the river. The divers sent down for the stones come up saying the river bed is full of hands.

temptation.label: Run your own ferry while the bridge is down.
temptation.text: A tidy profit, as long as the bridge stays down a while. Nobody need know whose ferries are carrying the trade.

triumph.text: The new span is finer than the old, and nobody looks down when crossing.

holds.text: Timber trestles carry the trade. The ferrymen charge double and will not cross after dark.

falters.text: Trade dwindles. The empty piers fill with people who stare at the water.

calamity.text: The river is a wall. The markets starve, and on still nights the hands below the water can be heard knocking on the hulls.
